question: How do the sibilants externalize the universe in manifest form?
premises: The same autonomous potency projects manifestation outward.
This projection appears as the triad of sibilants śa, ṣa, and sa.
In the phoneme sa the universe shines forth clearly.
inference: The sibilants, culminating in sa, are the phonemic form in which the universe becomes outwardly manifest.
uncertainties: The distinct roles of śa and ṣa are not differentiated in this verse.
plain_english: Making itself external and clearly projected, it abides as the triad śa, ṣa, and sa; and from that very basis the universe shines forth clearly in sa.
